question: Create a network analysis of the top 50 borrowers and lenders, and who they were borrowing from or lending to.
title: Who owed whom: top 50 network
understood: Borrowers = debtors in de dare entries (and the payers of the payments that follow); lenders = the creditor written in the entry, or the account holder when none is written.
limits: No creditor is written in any tagged MPAP 4 entry, so every link runs to the assumed account holder (the heirs of Deo di Vanni): the network shows who owed the estate, not lending between people.

answer.headline: In the tagged pages of MPAP 4 the network is a star: 74 debtors and institutions all owe the heirs of Deo di Vanni, so there is no lending between people to analyse yet.
answer.answer:
The 83 debts and payments with a tagged debtor on the 10 tagged pages involve 76 parties [all] [net]. No entry names its creditor. Every debt therefore runs to the account holder, the heirs of Deo di Vanni (assumed; dashed links), who are owed 75 debts, ƒ 335.66 and ℔ 342.17 in the two currencies [net] [by_creditor]. The top 50 is in practice everyone, and the picture is one hub with spokes, not a web of borrowers and lenders.

The largest debtors in florins are Bartolo di Nese, vinattiere (ƒ 176), Leonardo di Donato (ƒ 25.69), Pagolo di Jacopo dell'Aressa (ƒ 24) and the Compagnia di Santa Maria da Carraia (ƒ 19.03) [by_debtor_fl]. In lire they are Bartolo di Nese (℔ 79.81), Domenicuccio d'Andrea, lavoratore (℔ 64.88), Miglino (℔ 24), then Antonio and Bartolomeo di Neri (℔ 23.23 each) [by_debtor_li]. Each total is a single debt and a single unchecked sum.

The payments do tie some debtors to the estate's agent. Pagolo di Jacopo dell'Aressa, the Compagnia di Carraia, the Opera di San Barnaba and Francesco di Detto each made 3–4 payments, received by Miniato di messer Arrigo as the heirs' attore [net]. Because Miniato is recorded as recipient, not creditor, he does not appear as a lender.

claims.text: Every debt with a tagged debtor runs to one creditor, the heirs of Deo di Vanni, and none names its creditor.
Bartolo di Nese, vinattiere, owes the largest sum in both currencies (ƒ 176; ℔ 79.81).
Four debtors (Pagolo di Jacopo dell'Aressa, Compagnia di S. Maria da Carraia, Opera di San Barnaba, Francesco di Detto) made 3–4 payments each.

caveats: Joint debts (e.g. Mino di Ciapo with Lorenza, Antonio and Cristofano di Sandro, ƒ 32) are shared equally among the debtors in totals and on the network.
followups: To see lending between people, tag creditors (role 'creditor') where an entry names one, or extract Deo's own books (libro giallo / rosso), where he is the lender to many.
Add a 'recipient' layer to the network so the estate's agents (Miniato di messer Arrigo) appear.
